subject: Banking
title: JPMorgan Buys Bear Stearns
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on JPMorgan Buys Bear Stearns.

hook.text: In March 2008, JPMorgan bought Bear Stearns for $2 per share. A year earlier, Bear Stearns traded at $170.

buildup.text: Bear Stearns was heavily exposed to mortgage-backed securities.

discovery.text: The Federal Reserve arranged the deal over a single weekend.

twist.text: The Fed guaranteed $30 billion of Bear's toxic assets to make JPMorgan accept the deal.

climax.text: Bear Stearns showed that a bank can go from solvent to dead in 72 hours when confidence vanishes.

punchline.text: $170 to $2 per share. A bank dies when trust evaporates.

quiz.question: How fast did Bear Stearns collapse?
options: Within a single weekend when funding confidence evaporated

details.summary: In March 2008, JPMorgan acquired Bear Stearns for just 10 dollars per share in a government-facilitated emergency sale, saving the investment bank from collapse and marking the first major casualty of the financial crisis.
details.whyItMatters: The Bear Stearns rescue was a preview of the 2008 crisis. The speed of its collapse, from solvent to bankrupt in 72 hours, showed how quickly confidence can evaporate in a leveraged financial institution.
takeaways: Bear Stearns went from seemingly stable to collapse in just 72 hours
JPMorgan paid 10 dollars per share for stock that traded at 170 a year earlier
The Federal Reserve provided 30 billion in guarantees to facilitate the deal

faq.question: Why did Bear Stearns collapse so quickly?
faq.answer: Bear Stearns relied heavily on short-term borrowing to fund long-term assets. When counterparties lost confidence and refused to lend overnight, the liquidity dried up in days. It was a classic bank run, just in wholesale markets.

faq.question: Why did the government help JPMorgan buy it?
faq.answer: Officials feared that a disorderly Bear Stearns bankruptcy would trigger a chain reaction across the financial system. The Fed guaranteed 30 billion in Bear's risky assets to make the deal attractive enough for JPMorgan to accept.
